audit.whatIsWrong: The chart read Ziggs / Ziggs / Ziggs / Ziggs / Skill / Skill / Skill, the exact inverse of the shape the mirror (nautilus__ziggs) settled on: Skill for Levels 1-3, Ziggs from Levels 4-5 onward.
audit.why: The early rows were built on the false premise that you out-range him from level 1. Dredge Line is 1150 and your Bouncing Bomb is 850 — he out-ranges your poke with his engage, so levels 1-3 are a hook coin-flip, not free farm. Your edge arrives once Hexplosive Minefield and the mana to spam it do, which is Levels 4-5 and later.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-2 to Skill (rating 6/10 -> 5/10), rows 4-6 to Ziggs, each as a matched phases[N].side + win[N] pair in one atomic group. Row 3 already read Ziggs. whys[0..2] and phases[0].why rewritten so the prose stops claiming an early range advantage that does not exist.

audit.why: Spike ladder is sound: level 6 Depth Charge (120/100/80s, 825 range, point-and-click) is his, first item and beyond are yours on wave-clear and artillery reach.
audit.corrected: No structural change; added the real Dredge Line timer to the level 3-5 spike instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (a) The page never states that Dredge Line out-ranges your Q. (b) Staggering Blow is called a 'stun' in wants.foe[1] — Riot's text says it roots. (c) dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[0].d were filler with no mechanic ('the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee', 'bread-and-butter play').
audit.why: 1150 vs 850 is the single most important number in the lane and it was absent. Root versus stun changes what you can still do while caught. And Titan's Wrath is a 12s flat-cooldown shield, which is the actual reason dumping a rotation into a full-HP Nautilus achieves nothing — a far better 'don't' than the generic one.
audit.corrected: 1150 written into spikes[0].text, phases[0].why, whys[0] and breakdown.cooldowns; Dredge Line's 14s and Titan's Wrath's 12s supplied; Staggering Blow corrected to a root.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Count it out loud if you must' with no number to count.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s — the longest punish window in his kit and the one you actually step up into. Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1, so a whiffed hook still does not license a commit if your W is down.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[2].d now carry 14s, 10s and 20s.

edits.before: Q bombs out-range every melee tool in the game — chunk Nautilus on every last-hit attempt, but respect early minion aggro.
edits.after: Dredge Line reaches 1150 — further than your 850 Q — so chunk him on last-hits from the far side and never hug the wall.

edits.before: You out-range hookless Nautilus at Lvl 1 and poke him freely.
edits.after: Dredge Line reaches 1150 to your 850 — level 1 is even.

edits.before: Lvl 2 he still has no way to reach you without a telegraphed hook.
edits.after: Lvl 2 stays even — one landed hook still flips the whole trade.

edits.before: Lvl 3 you punish every Dredge Line whiff with Q and autos.
edits.after: Lvl 3 is a coin flip on one hook: whiff and you punish.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Hook): matchup-defining — His only real engage — dodge it and the lane is free. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Satchel has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Hook): matchup-defining — his only real engage at 14s, and it out-ranges your Q at 1150. - Your W Satchel has one job at 20s: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.

edits.before: Nautilus spends Dredge Line (Hook) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 and still 10s maxed — a whiffed hook is your whole window to step up.

edits.before: That’s Nautilus’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Titan's Wrath shields him every 12s — chip into it and you gain nothing.

edits.before: Nautilus lives or dies on landing Dredge Line — sidestep the hook and he has nothing, so bait it with a jink then punish the whiff cooldown with Q Bouncing Bomb and Short Fuse autos while he's exposed.
edits.after: Nautilus lives or dies on Dredge Line, and it reaches 1150 to your 850 — you cannot simply stand outside it. Bait the hook, then punish the 14s whiff window with Q and Short Fuse autos.

edits.before: Chain Staggering Blow stun into R Depth Charge
edits.after: Chain Staggering Blow's root into R Depth Charge

notes: Chart proposed as six matched side/win pairs plus one rating, as one atomic group, following the shape the mirror already settled. The decisive correction here is that Dredge Line (1150) out-ranges Bouncing Bomb (850) — the old early-game prose was built on the opposite assumption. Kit flag misfire noted by the mirror and honoured here: ziggs.json tags Satchel Charge with percentHealth, but Riot's text says only magic damage, knockback and the turret hexplode, so nothing percent-health was written. Not asserted (not in the kit text): whether Depth Charge can be dodged with Satchel Charge's self-knockback, whether Staggering Blow's root is reduced by tenacity, and whether Dredge Line's terrain-pull can be blocked.
